azure-digital-twins.title: What is Azure Digital Twins? – Microsoft Learn
azure-digital-twins.notes: Azure Digital Twins is a platform-as-a-service offering for building twin graphs from digital models of whole environments such as buildings, factories, farms, energy networks, railways, stadiums or cities. Types are described in the JSON-like Digital Twins Definition Language through properties, components and relationships, and ready-made industry ontologies exist. Concrete twins are created from these models and linked by relationships into a graph, which can be explored in the Azure Digital Twins Explorer. Data arrives from IoT Hub, REST APIs or connectors such as Logic Apps, and events update the graph, with custom processing often done in Azure Functions. A query API lets you search by property values, relationships and model information, while event routes forward data through Event Hubs, Event Grid or Service Bus to downstream services. A data history feature records graph updates into an Azure Data Explorer cluster, and 3D Scenes Studio, still in preview, maps 3D elements to twins. The page does not list prerequisites or licensing, and it points to a separate article for service limits. It also distinguishes the service from Digital Twin Builder in Fabric and from IoT Hub device twins.

azure-iot-edge.title: What is Azure IoT Edge – Microsoft Learn
azure-iot-edge.notes: Azure IoT Edge is a device-focused runtime for deploying, running and monitoring containerized Linux workloads, and it is a feature of Azure IoT Hub. Its aim is to move analytics closer to devices so decisions can be made quickly, even offline, and so raw data can be cleaned and aggregated locally before only the results travel to the cloud, which lowers bandwidth use. The solution has three parts: IoT Edge modules, which are Docker-compatible containers running Azure services, partner services or custom code and can be chained into a pipeline; the IoT Edge runtime on each device, which installs and updates modules, keeps them running, enforces security standards and reports module health; and a cloud interface for remote monitoring and management. It is available in the free and standard IoT Hub tiers, the free tier being meant for testing and evaluation only. Linux is the native platform, with Windows supported through IoT Edge for Linux on Windows. Typical uses include anomaly detection on production lines, gateway devices that aggregate local data, and running machine learning or Stream Analytics at the edge. The page also notes which long-term-support versions are current and which have reached or will reach end of support.

azure-relay.title: What is Azure Relay? – Microsoft Learn
azure-relay.notes: Azure Relay lets you expose services running in a corporate network to the public cloud without opening a firewall port or making invasive changes to the network, and a relay can be limited to a single application endpoint on one machine, unlike a VPN. The on-premises service opens an outbound connection to the relay and creates a bidirectional socket for a given address. Clients send traffic to that address, and the relay forwards it over the socket, so clients need no knowledge of the service location and the local service needs no inbound ports. Supported scenarios include one-way, request/response and peer-to-peer messaging, internet-scale event distribution, and unbuffered bidirectional sockets across network boundaries. There are two features that share a gateway but are implemented differently. Hybrid Connections builds on HTTP and WebSockets, works across platforms and languages including .NET and Node.js, and replaces the Hybrid Connections feature of BizTalk Services. WCF Relay uses Windows Communication Foundation for remote procedure calls, works only with the full .NET Framework rather than .NET Core, and is described as a legacy option. The page does not cover pricing, quotas or service limits and refers readers to the FAQ.

azure-spot-virtual-machines.title: Azure Spot Virtual Machines – Microsoft Learn
azure-spot-virtual-machines.notes: Azure Spot Virtual Machines run on spare Azure capacity at a reduced price, and Azure can evict them whenever it needs the capacity back. They suit workloads that tolerate interruption, such as batch processing, dev/test environments and stateless processing. Two eviction policies exist: deallocate, the default, keeps the VM in a stopped-deallocated state, though redeployment is not guaranteed, and the disks still incur storage cost and the cores still count against quota; delete removes both the VM and its disks. A maximum price can be set in US dollars per hour, and a value of minus one means the VM is never evicted for price reasons. Scheduled events can give a best-effort warning shortly before eviction, and price and eviction-rate history is visible in the portal and through Azure Resource Graph. Spot VMs draw on their own quota pool. They are offered under several agreement types, including Enterprise Agreement, pay-as-you-go and Cloud Solution Provider. There is no SLA or availability guarantee, B-series and promo sizes are unsupported, a VM cannot be converted between Spot and standard, and changing the max price requires deallocation. Microsoft advises standard VMs where capacity is needed immediately.

azure-stack-edge.title: Azure Stack Edge documentation – Microsoft Learn
azure-stack-edge.notes: Azure Stack Edge is a family of devices that bring Azure capabilities to edge locations, covering compute, storage, networking and hardware-accelerated machine learning. The overview page also frames it as a way to move data into Azure over the network, with offline transfer as an alternative described in the Azure Storage documentation. The product overview lists Pro 2, Pro GPU, Pro R and Mini R models, while the release notes additionally mention a Pro FPGA model. Management areas named on the page are edge shares, edge compute and edge storage accounts. Workloads that can be deployed include GPU modules from the marketplace, virtual machines through the portal or templates, IoT Edge modules, and Kubernetes via IoT Edge, kubectl or Azure Arc with GitOps. The page is a landing page that links to model-specific system requirements, deployment checklists, limits, device return and support contact information. It does not itself state licensing, pricing, hardware specifications or concrete limits, so those details have to be taken from the linked subpages.

azure-storage-account.title: Storage account overview – Microsoft Learn
azure-storage-account.notes: An Azure storage account contains all Azure Storage data objects, namely blobs, files, queues and tables, and provides a unique namespace reachable worldwide over HTTP or HTTPS. Account types include standard general-purpose v2, which Microsoft recommends for most scenarios, plus premium block blobs, premium file shares supporting SMB and NFS, and premium page blobs. Older types such as general-purpose v1 and Blob Storage are being phased out, and classic accounts have been retired. The type cannot be changed after creation, so switching means creating a new account and copying the data. Redundancy options range from locally redundant to geo-zone-redundant storage, with read-access variants, depending on type and region. Names must be unique across Azure, three to twenty-four characters long, and use only lowercase letters and digits. Data is encrypted on the server side automatically. Billing depends on region, account type, access tier, capacity, redundancy, transactions and data egress. Accounts can move between subscriptions or resource groups, while a region change means copying data, for example with AzCopy. Typical uses include cloud-native apps, analytics, backup and archiving, and machine learning.

client-credentials-flow.title: OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow – Microsoft identity platform
client-credentials-flow.notes: The OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant, sometimes called two-legged OAuth, lets a confidential client such as a web service authenticate with its own credentials instead of acting for a user, which makes it suited to background daemons and service accounts. Before requesting a token, the app must be authorized, either through an access control list kept by the resource server or through application permissions, also called app roles, which a tenant administrator grants in Microsoft Entra ID. Delegated permissions cannot be used because no user is involved. The app posts to the token endpoint with the client credentials grant type and a scope made of the resource identifier plus the default suffix, and only one resource may be named per request. Authentication can use a client secret, a certificate-signed assertion, or a federated credential from an external identity provider. The response contains a bearer access token and its lifetime, and no refresh token is issued, so the app requests a new token on expiry. Credentials must never sit in source code or distributed native apps. Microsoft recommends using MSAL rather than raw protocol calls.

cloud-solution-provider.title: Cloud Solution Provider program overview – Microsoft Partner Center
cloud-solution-provider.notes: The Cloud Solution Provider authorization allows partners to sell Microsoft cloud services and other offers, including server software and perpetual software, to customers. Two models exist: the indirect model, where a partner works through a distributor, and the direct-bill model, where Microsoft bills the partner directly. The page lists benefits such as closer customer relationships, added revenue from deployment and support services, bundling Microsoft products with industry solutions, and control over the full customer lifecycle. All CSP partners must pass business verification, repeat it every year, and keep a current partner profile in Partner Center. Indirect partners need active membership in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program, a partner location account ID, authority to accept legal agreements and a relationship with an authorized distributor. Direct-bill partners face stricter criteria: a period as an indirect reseller, a minimum trailing revenue amount, a capabilities assessment covering billing, provisioning and support, a managed service or own solution offering, a solution partner designation, security requirements and an advanced support plan. Customers must accept the Microsoft Customer Agreement before ordering.

copilot-plus-pc.title: Copilot+ PCs developer guide – Microsoft Learn
copilot-plus-pc.notes: Copilot+ PCs are a class of Windows 11 devices built around a neural processing unit, a specialized chip for AI-heavy work such as real-time translation and image generation. Many of the new Windows AI features require an NPU delivering more than 40 trillion operations per second. Running AI tasks on the NPU is described as more efficient than on the CPU or GPU, which helps battery life, and Windows 11 distributes work across CPU, GPU and NPU depending on what suits each task. The Task Manager shows NPU utilization. The page names Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite as an example chip and lists devices from several manufacturers, with support for other chip families described as arriving later. For developers, Windows ML is recommended; it builds on ONNX Runtime, detects the hardware, loads a fitting execution provider and falls back to GPU or CPU when needed. Models can come from Qualcomm AI Hub or the ONNX Model Zoo, or be optimized with the Olive tool. Because most NPUs handle low-precision integer formats, models often need quantization. Some Windows AI APIs are not yet shipped and are tied to an upcoming Windows App SDK release. The page gives no pricing or licensing information.

copilot-prompt-gallery.title: Copilot Prompt Gallery – Microsoft Learn
copilot-prompt-gallery.notes: The Copilot Prompt Gallery is a resource of Microsoft-created prompts, videos and articles meant to help people understand and use Microsoft Copilot effectively. It is reachable from within Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat, and it lets users save and share prompts across teams to encourage consistency and collaboration. The gallery has three areas: Suggested prompts curated by Microsoft, Your Prompts that a user creates and saves, and Teams prompts shared by a team. Each prompt includes hints on personalizing and extending it. Opening it from Copilot requires authentication; people who are not signed in can only browse the Microsoft-created prompts on the web and need to sign in to try them. Microsoft prompts come from a public catalog, while user and group prompts are stored in collections within the Microsoft 365 Substrate data store inside the tenant boundary, encrypted and reachable only through Substrate APIs. Administrators get analytics and reporting on saved, liked and shared prompts and on prompts shared with a team, with a separate article covering export. The page does not state license requirements, concrete limits, regional availability or supported languages.

credential-guard.title: Credential Guard overview – Microsoft Learn
credential-guard.notes: Credential Guard protects against credential theft by shielding NTLM password hashes, Kerberos ticket-granting tickets and credentials that applications store as domain credentials. It relies on virtualization-based security to isolate these secrets so that only privileged system software can reach them, which makes attacks such as pass-the-hash and pass-the-ticket harder. Even malware running with administrator rights cannot extract secrets protected this way. VBS and Secure Boot are required, while a TPM and UEFI lock are recommended. Hyper-V guests must be generation 2, and the host needs an IOMMU. The feature is supported on Windows Enterprise and Education editions with matching E3, E5, A3 or A5 licenses, but not on Pro. It is enabled by default on recent Windows 11 and Windows Server releases for domain-joined devices that meet the requirements, without UEFI lock, and Microsoft advises against enabling it on domain controllers. It does not protect the Active Directory database or the SAM. Applications that need Kerberos DES, unconstrained delegation, TGT extraction or NTLMv1 break, and some others, such as those using CredSSP, MS-CHAPv2 or digest authentication, expose credentials. Attackers are expected to adopt new techniques.

dax-user-defined-functions.title: DAX user-defined functions – Microsoft Learn
dax-user-defined-functions.notes: DAX user-defined functions are reusable pieces of DAX logic declared with the FUNCTION keyword. They are first-class model objects that appear under a Functions node in the model explorer, and they let teams centralize business rules and change calculations more safely over time. A function can take parameters, optionally with default expressions, typed as scalar, table or reference kinds, and each parameter is passed either eagerly by value or lazily as an expression. Type-check functions such as ISSTRING and information functions such as TABLEOF and NAMEOF help write flexible logic, and JSDoc-style comments beginning with three slashes feed IntelliSense. Functions can be defined and tested in DAX query view or TMDL view, edited in the model explorer, and live in a functions file inside Power BI projects. They can be called from measures, calculated columns, visual calculations and other functions. A compatibility level of 1702 or higher is required. Limitations include no recursion, no overloading, no explicit return type, no hiding in the model, and only limited IntelliSense in some tools. Visual calculations can pass only fields from the visual. The page gives no licensing information.

dotnet-aspire.title: .NET Aspire overview – Microsoft Learn
dotnet-aspire.notes: The page describes .NET Aspire as an opinionated, cloud-ready stack for building observable, production-ready distributed applications, delivered as a set of NuGet packages that each address a specific cloud-native concern. It has three main parts. Orchestration runs and connects multiple projects and their dependencies in local development, composing an app from .NET projects, containers, executables and cloud resources while handling service discovery and connection strings. Components are NuGet packages for common services such as Redis or PostgreSQL that expose standardized interfaces and bring health checks and telemetry. Tooling provides project templates and support in Visual Studio and the dotnet command line. A typical solution contains the app itself, an AppHost project for orchestration and a ServiceDefaults project, and two starter templates exist, one minimal and one with sample UI and API projects. The ServiceDefaults call wires up OpenTelemetry logging, metrics and tracing, default health check endpoints and service discovery for HttpClient. Orchestration is intended mainly for local development and does not replace production platforms such as Kubernetes. The page does not cover prerequisites or licensing and only lists a few example components.

dynamics-365-accounts-receivable.title: Accounts receivable overview – Dynamics 365 Finance – Microsoft Learn
dynamics-365-accounts-receivable.notes: Accounts receivable in Dynamics 365 Finance is used to track customer invoices and incoming payments. It can create customer invoices from sales orders or packing slips, as well as free text invoices that are not tied to a sales order, and it supports recurring invoices. Payments can be recorded through several methods, including bills of exchange, cash, checks, credit cards and electronic payments. Centralized payments let a payment entered in one legal entity be applied on behalf of others. Further features cover interest handling with interest codes and interest notes, SEPA direct debits with mandates, credit card setup with authorization and capture, partial payments, cash discounts and customer refunds. Setup involves customer groups, customers, posting profiles, collection letters, parameters and the closing of accounts receivable. Subscription billing manages recurring revenue opportunities through billing schedules. Credit and collections gives a central collections page, where managers oversee the process and collectors work from customer lists built on predefined criteria. The page does not mention licensing, general prerequisites or limitations beyond setup steps.

co-management.title: What is co-management? – Configuration Manager – Microsoft Learn
co-management.notes: Co-management means managing Windows devices with Configuration Manager and Microsoft Intune at the same time. It lets organizations keep their existing Configuration Manager investment while using cloud capabilities such as conditional access based on device compliance. Workloads can be moved to Intune one at a time or gradually, including compliance policies, Windows update policies, resource access policies, endpoint protection, device configuration, Office Click-to-Run apps and client apps. Anything not switched, and any feature co-management does not support, stays with Configuration Manager. A workload can first be piloted with a separate device collection, and a dashboard helps monitor co-managed devices. Existing clients reach co-management through hybrid Microsoft Entra join and Intune enrollment, while new internet-based devices join Entra ID, enroll automatically and receive the Configuration Manager client. Requirements include Entra ID P1 or P2 licensing, an Intune license for the administrator, a supported Current Branch version and devices that are Entra joined or hybrid joined. Devices that are only Entra registered are not supported. Co-management covers Windows devices only.

data-access-governance-reports.title: Data access governance reports – SharePoint in Microsoft 365 – Microsoft Learn
data-access-governance-reports.notes: Data access governance reports help administrators control access to SharePoint data by surfacing sites that may be overshared or hold sensitive content, so suitable security and compliance policies can be applied. They are opened in the SharePoint admin center under Reports and need SharePoint administrator rights. The requirements of SharePoint Advanced Management apply, and the reports are unavailable for Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet. Organizations with Microsoft 365 E5 alone get the reports but not snapshot reports or remediation actions. Snapshot reports show the current state: site permissions across the organization, site permissions for a given user, sensitivity labels applied to files, and content shared through broad groups such as Everyone except external users. Activity reports cover recent sharing link creation and sharing with Everyone except external users. Microsoft suggests running snapshot reports first as a baseline and activity reports afterwards for ongoing monitoring. Without Advanced Management, data collection must be switched on for activity reports. Reports may fail when concealed user, group and site names are enabled in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

dynamics-365-intelligent-order-managemen.title: Intelligent Order Management overview – Microsoft Learn
dynamics-365-intelligent-order-managemen.notes: Dynamics 365 Intelligent Order Management is a cloud-based solution for orchestrating orders through to fulfillment. It is built as a Microsoft Dataverse application that shares the common data model with other Dynamics 365 apps, and the page states it has no dependency on them. It supports business-to-consumer, direct-to-consumer and business-to-business scenarios and strategies such as buy online and ship, or buy online and collect, while connecting different e-commerce systems and fulfillment partners. Its parts include an app giving a unified view of orders and fulfillment status regardless of source, providers that wrap API calls between systems as actions and build on Power Automate connectors, an orchestration layer configured with designer tools that business users can change, an Inventory Visibility service for real-time stock across legal entities, a Fulfillment Optimization service that chooses the best fulfillment location, for example by cost or distance, and Insights with prebuilt Power BI dashboards. First-party providers exist for Dynamics 365 applications, and customers or partners can develop their own. The page gives no license models, prices, system requirements or explicit technical limits.

dynamics-365-sales-accelerator.title: Sales accelerator overview – Dynamics 365 Sales – Microsoft Learn
dynamics-365-sales-accelerator.notes: Sales accelerator is a capability of Dynamics 365 Sales that gives sellers a tailored workspace for prioritizing customers and streamlining their approach. It gathers information from several sources and aims to reduce the time spent finding the next best customer and working out whom to contact, when and how. It builds a prioritized pipeline, supplies context and offers automated recommendations within a sales sequence. The intelligent work list shows the next best leads or opportunities with sales-relevant details and customer context. With the sequence designer, sales managers configure sequences of activities that define steps for daily planning, and sellers can also create and manage their own sequences. By default it is available in the Sales Hub app with limited functionality, showing work list items from the timeline of contact, opportunity, lead and account records along with search, filter and sort. For the full feature set, an administrator must configure the sales accelerator workspace. It is not supported on mobile devices such as tablets and phones. The page does not mention licensing, costs, data sources or the recommendation mechanism.

dynamics-365-commerce.title: Dynamics 365 Commerce overview – Microsoft Learn
dynamics-365-commerce.notes: Dynamics 365 Commerce builds on the established capabilities of Dynamics 365 Retail and is an omnichannel solution that brings together back office, in-store, call center and digital experiences. The page names goals such as stronger customer loyalty through personalized interactions, higher revenue through better employee productivity, and lower costs through more efficient operations and supply chain. Components include digital storefronts with integrated web authoring tools, a headless commerce and marketing platform that manages content, promotions, inventory and pricing across channels, clienteling with customer profiles and history, loyalty programs, AI-based recommendations and customer insights. Omnichannel features cover search, product reviews, wish lists, gift cards, multiple payment methods and pickup or delivery options. Further areas are merchandising, inventory management, distributed order management, pricing and promotions, and analytics. AI features address accessible websites, payment fraud protection and moderation of user-generated content. Documentation sections cover channels, products, orders, customers, finance and extensibility through the Retail SDK. The page names no prerequisites, license models or limitations.

dynamics-365-procurement-and-sourcing.title: Procurement and sourcing overview – Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management – Microsoft Learn
dynamics-365-procurement-and-sourcing.notes: The procurement and sourcing area of Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management covers the whole path from identifying the need for products and services through purchasing, receiving and invoicing to paying vendors, and processes can be adapted with purchasing policies and workflows. Demand and vendor selection use requisitions, product catalogs, spending limits, approval workflows, budget funds, requests for quotation that vendors can answer in the vendor portal, simpler purchase inquiries and approved vendor lists. Purchase orders can originate from planned orders, requisitions, blanket agreements or manual entry. Pricing and terms rely on trade agreements, purchase agreements and rebate agreements. Delivery features include delivery schedules, direct delivery from sales orders, intercompany orders, supplementary items and charges. Goods arrive through arrival registration and product receipts, and vendor invoices are matched to receipts before payables and payment. Reports include spend analysis and vendor performance. Limitations noted: purchase inquiry is disabled for vendors set up for the vendor portal, and orders under an approval workflow cannot proceed without approval. The page names no license requirements.

fabric-data-factory.title: What is Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric? – Microsoft Learn
fabric-data-factory.notes: Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric is a data integration service described as the next generation of Azure Data Factory. It brings scattered data from databases, files, cloud services and legacy systems together, cleans it and prepares it for analytics in a lakehouse or data warehouse, orchestrating movement and transformation from one interface. It connects to well over a hundred data sources, including multicloud and hybrid ones through on-premises gateways. For moving data, a copy job is the preferred option and handles bulk, incremental and change data capture copies, copy activity offers manual control over parallelism, and mirroring keeps a near-real-time replica of an operational database in OneLake. Transformations run through pipeline activities such as notebooks, Spark job definitions, stored procedures and SQL scripts, through Dataflow Gen2 with a low-code interface, or through dbt jobs against a Fabric data warehouse. Orchestration includes schedules, event-based triggers, control flow in the pipeline designer and Apache Airflow DAGs. Copilot can create pipelines and dataflows from natural-language prompts and explain errors. Both ETL and ELT patterns are supported. A Fabric tenant account with an active subscription and a workspace with Fabric enabled are needed.

fabric-warehouse-snapshots.title: Warehouse snapshots in Microsoft Fabric – Microsoft Learn
fabric-warehouse-snapshots.notes: A warehouse snapshot in Microsoft Fabric is a read-only representation of a warehouse item at a specific point in time, created as a child item of its parent warehouse. It gives analysts a consistent view of the data while real-time updates continue and protects reports from partial changes made by ETL processes. Stated uses include a stable warehouse version, ETL consistency, historical analysis, reporting accuracy and regularly refreshed snapshots. The snapshot timestamp can be rolled forward on demand, instantly and atomically, and queries already running finish against the data version they started with. Consumers can use the same connection string. A snapshot has no storage of its own and relies on the source warehouse. T-SQL access is limited to queries, with no data changes and no DDL apart from updating the timestamp. Admins, members and contributors can create and manage snapshots, while viewers can query them. Security settings are applied in the source warehouse and take effect immediately. Limitations include that schema changes in the parent carry over and can break reports, retention is bounded by the parent warehouse, Power BI can use only DirectQuery or Import rather than Direct Lake, and snapshots are not supported on a lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint.

instance-metadata-service.title: Azure Instance Metadata Service – Microsoft Learn
instance-metadata-service.notes: The Azure Instance Metadata Service provides information about running virtual machines and scale set instances, such as SKU, storage, network configuration and upcoming maintenance events, which helps with managing and configuring them. It is a REST API on a non-routable address that can only be reached from inside the VM, and the traffic never leaves the host. It supports Linux and Windows VMs and flexible scale sets. Endpoint categories include attested data that proves a VM runs in Azure, tokens for managed identities, instance metadata covering compute, network and storage plus tags and user data, load balancer metadata, scheduled events and a list of supported API versions. Requests must carry a specific metadata header, include an API version parameter, run over the primary network interface and bypass any proxy. Only GET over plain HTTP is supported. Typical uses are retrieving a unique VM identifier, fault and update domains for replica placement, tags, the Azure environment, and signed attestation documents. The API is unauthenticated and open to every process in the VM, so sensitive data does not belong in it, and a rate limit applies per VM, returning an error when exceeded. The page names no license requirements for the service itself.

foundry-model-catalog.title: Model catalog and collections in Microsoft Foundry – Microsoft Learn
foundry-model-catalog.notes: The model catalog in the Foundry portal is a hub for discovering, evaluating and deploying models for generative AI applications, covering foundation, reasoning, small language, multimodal, domain-specific and industry models. It has two categories. Models sold by Azure are hosted and sold by Microsoft under Microsoft Product Terms, with Microsoft support, enterprise SLAs and a responsible AI review. Models from partners and community come from third parties, research labs and contributors, are billed through the Azure Marketplace, and are supported by their providers rather than Microsoft. Users can search and filter by collection, region, deployment option, lifecycle stage, supported features and inference task, compare models using a leaderboard and benchmarks, and open a model card with quick facts, details, deployments, benchmarks and license tabs. Deployment is either managed compute on dedicated virtual machines, billed by VM core hours, or serverless deployment through a Microsoft-hosted API, billed mostly by tokens. Managed compute needs VM quota and a hub-based project. Typical uses are copilots, agents, retrieval-augmented generation and fine-tuning. Content filtering is not available for embedding and time-series models.

global-secure-access.title: What is Global Secure Access? – Microsoft Entra – Microsoft Learn
global-secure-access.notes: Global Secure Access is the umbrella for Microsoft Entra Internet Access and Microsoft Entra Private Access, Microsoft's security service edge offering, managed centrally in the Microsoft Entra admin center and built on zero-trust principles. It aims to give identity-aware access control and visibility for users and devices inside and outside the office and to converge network, identity and endpoint access controls. Internet Access acts as an identity-based secure web gateway, forwarding traffic through a user-specific profile via a desktop client or a remote network such as a branch office, with traffic logs, conditional access integration and web content filtering by category or domain name. Its Microsoft services variant adds a compliant network check, universal tenant restrictions and source IP restoration for sign-in logs. Private Access provides zero trust network access to private resources without a classic VPN, including per-app access for TCP and UDP applications, private DNS and single sign-on for private apps. Licensing generally needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 per user, with the services also available in the Entra Suite. Several capabilities are marked as preview, and not every feature is available in every traffic profile.
